goal: Install the Transformers dependencies from the README (a CPU build of torch is fine) and make the README's single-page Transformers inference work on this CPU-only machine. The hidden test loads the model with AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2', trust_remote_code=True) and AutoModel.from_pretrained('baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2', trust_remote_code=True, use_safetensors=True, torch_dtype=torch.float32).eval() with no .cuda() call (there is no GPU), then runs model.infer(tokenizer, image_file=<a page image>, output_path=<dir>, save_results=True) on a simple text image and expects correct OCR text back.
check: A hidden script generates an image containing known text lines, runs model.infer on CPU through the standard HF loading path, and verifies the returned text contains the expected words.

eam version could replace the patched code.

Each page takes about 2.5–3.5 minutes on 4 cores. Memory peaks around 12.7 GB of the 16 GB, so a very large page or a smaller machine could still run out. The two test images were 1000×600 and A4 size (1240×1754).

`setup.sh` contains the patch script inline, so it doesn't need anything else from `/work`. The details are in `NOTES.md` and `REPORT.json`.
